worst_three.where: The Tony Blair Institute sums up the bargain
worst_three.problem: Each section break here has no spoken pause, so the listener gets 75 to 100 words in a row, running straight from one section into the next, and loses the thread.
worst_three.fix: Add [Pause] before every [Section] marker in the script, especially after 'limits on Chinese collaboration.', after 'forty per cent of them were Arabic.', after 'AI runs on electricity, and lots of it.' and after 'without another party's permission.' Also add a [Pause] inside the long Brookings/IISS/Carnegie run, after 'digital authoritarianism.'

worst_three.problem: Within the labelled view, Wissam's opinion and the think tanks' sourced position run together, so the listener can't tell whether 'Own what's critical. Steer the rest.' is Wissam's view or a reported finding.
worst_three.fix: Close the view first: 'That's my view.' [Pause]. Then put the sourced line after it as reported fact: 'For the record, Brookings, Carnegie and the Tony Blair Institute all describe the goal as "managed interdependence": own what's critical, steer the rest.' Also resolve the [DRAFT VIEW] marker with the founder before recording.

worst_three.problem: Two dates and a power figure in one sentence blur together on first hearing.
worst_three.fix: Split it: 'G42 said the first 200 megawatts should go live in 2026.' Drop 'In May 2025' here, because the previous paragraph already dates the unveiling to May 2025.
